families.name: loxilb_ai_tokens_missing_total
families.activation_precondition: AI traffic whose responses carry no usage object. The family partitions on how the response was charged, not on a single branch: a STREAMED response falls back to the estimate net (RecordTokenUsage estimated arm, which also feeds loxilb_ai_tokens_estimated_total), while a NON-STREAMED one is reported by RecordTokenUsageMissing and charged nothing. This family is therefore a superset of the estimated one, and the gap between them is the uncharged non-streamed half. Restricted to SUCCESSFUL (2xx) responses: an error body carries no usage object either, but it completed no work, so it is not an accounting hole and the data plane does not report it. Without that test a backend outage would drive the family harder than the condition it reports. The reason label splits the uncharged half by the BOUNDARY the report fired at, because that half was covering two opposite policy cases in one number: response_complete is the H1 keep-alive reset, where the client sent the next request on the same connection and the exchange demonstrably finished, so a 2xx without usage is the backend omitting it; connection_close is the H1/H2 teardown sweep, where the status was seen and the connection ended before any usage was read, which a client taking the 2xx and cutting reaches identically; h2_stream_close is an HTTP/2 stream close, which nghttp2 runs for a finished response and for one aborted after its headers with no error code plumbed through, so it establishes neither. stream_estimated is the charged arm. Only response_complete proves completion, and the names say so rather than guessing. Driving one reason does NOT activate the others: a single-request-per-connection arm produces connection_close only, and response_complete needs two requests on one kept-alive connection.

writer_sources.note: the streamed half only, charged from the estimate net, and the sole writer of reason=stream_estimated. The non-streamed half is RecordTokenUsageMissing (api/prometheus/ai_metrics.go:561), reached from the cgo export llb_ai_record_usage_missing (pkg/loxinet/ai_gateway_dp.go:1498), which charges nothing and writes the other three reasons -- so this family must never be read as a subset of loxilb_ai_tokens_estimated_total. It is a second writer chain rather than a hop on this one, and writer_sources holds a single ordered chain, which is why it is recorded here in prose. The reason vocabulary is closed on the Go side by boundTokenMissingReason (api/prometheus/ai_metrics.go:513), which collapses anything it does not know onto "unknown": the value crosses cgo from a separately versioned repo, so pin skew is a real way to reach an unlisted value and an allow-list is what keeps the label bounded. The data-plane spellings live in loxilb-ebpf/common/sockproxy_ai_gw.h (LLB_AI_UMISS_*) and must be changed on both sides together. families.verification_evidence: COMMITTED GATE since 2026-09-21: cicd/vllm-pd-disagg validation.sh phase N, 47 asserts. The scenario is named in ai-gateway-sanity.yml on the default path, so this family is scored on every PR. Supersedes the 2026-09-16 D-14 hand-run (image d14-u24, sha256:4e262e1e6dd6) -- a one-off runtime observation on the M08 bed with no standing gate; that text is preserved in the campaign resume doc. THE ORACLE IS A MATRIX, NOT A RATE. Each arm puts the fixture in a state that can produce exactly ONE outcome and asserts the matching child moves inside a band, while every OTHER child is flat -- including the child that carried the previous arm, which must FREEZE. N1 states the activation-P pre-create separately and labels it as the pre-create property and NOT as liveness, because all seven children read 0 on a gateway whose scraper never ran a single poll. N2 404 -> http_error; N3 200 + the recognized vLLM series -> ok with http_error FROZEN; N4 200 carrying nothing recognized -> unparseable with ok AND http_error frozen; N5 one mock's listener stopped -> unreachable AND http_error in the SAME window, each inside its own share of a tick, plus a conservation identity stated only alongside those two arm-specific deltas; N6 that mock restarted -> unreachable FREEZES while http_error resumes over the whole population. body_error, bad_request and unknown are not reachable from a live scrape of a well-behaved listener and are asserted FLAT throughout rather than claimed as runtime-covered; they stay unit-covered by TestRecordWorkerScrapeFoldsUnknown and siblings. THE DRIVE SHAPE IS DERIVED: N0 reads the gateway's own loadbalancer list and counts endpoints over pd_disagg rules (10 polls per 10s tick from three rules) and each endpoint's multiplicity, so N5 predicts the stopped endpoint's share (l3ep4 = 2 of 10) separately from the rest (8 of 10). A band built on a hardcoded population would redden a correct product after any config change. THE WINDOW IS MEASURED, not nominal: every reading is bracketed by a timestamp before and after the /metrics curl, the tick floor taken from the narrowest possible elapsed window and the ceiling from the widest. The first bed run put every reading exactly on the lower band edge, which is where a slow scrape would have produced a false red; that was fixed before any run was treated as evidence. FIXTURE: mock_vllm.py gained a runtime metrics-mode knob (absent | vllm | garbage) on its existing admin server plus a /metrics route. Default 'absent' is byte-identical to the historical behaviour -- the path falls through to the same 404 -- so phases A-M and the three other scenarios that docker-cp this file are unaffected, and phase N restores it on the way out. GREEN: full suite 134P/0F on ws-u24 (sha256:5723bfafa78c, built from main 307b4c71). Readings: N2 http_error +22, N3 ok +26 with http_error frozen at 481, N4 unparseable +24 with ok frozen at 40 and http_error still 481, N5 unreachable +5 and http_error +19 in one window summing to 24 of a 20..30 window, N6 unreachable frozen at 27 while http_error +28. RETENTION: phase N was also run TWICE against the SAME gateway with NO reconfiguration (the run_local path re-runs config.sh, which hands each run an empty gateway and proves nothing about retention). Both 47P/0F while the family's running totals climbed to http_error 651, ok 79, unparseable 79, unreachable 11 -- every delta still inside its band on a counter carrying a full suite's history. RED TWINS, all three predicted IN WRITING before the first twin build finished, and all three matching exactly -- same count, same arms, no others. Twin P (wstwinp-u24 sha256:b1c4a5bc4c27, RecordWorkerScrape stops incrementing, diff 11 lines) 127P/7F: the seven reds are every BAND arm, while every FLAT arm, every FREEZE arm and N1 stayed GREEN -- TN4d reads 'http_error flat at 0'. So the freezes cannot detect a dead writer and the bands carry that claim alone. Twin Q (wstwinq-u24 sha256:a8d177d48cb0, every outcome charged to result=\"ok\", diff 12 lines) 123P/11F: the whole of N3 passed, 9 of 9, under a mutation that has destroyed the family's meaning -- in mode=vllm the correct child IS ok, it does move, and http_error is legitimately frozen. N2 is what catches it. Twin R (wstwinr-u24 sha256:4a9e9be54966, the outcome decided on the STATUS LINE alone so a 200 is always ok, default hot-path branch only, diff 16 lines) 131P/3F: N2, N3, N5 and N6 all passed in full and only N4 went red, which is what shows N4 is not redundant with N3 -- same status code, same transport, one field of the body changed. Measured: delta 6.0 == 6 PARKED log lines; pd_admission_shed asserted FLAT because its branch is unreachable at depth 2, so the delta identifies which branch ran; 3 overflow log lines and 3 client receipts of 429 pd_overloaded, the parked requests correctly answering nothing because parking is hold-don't-drop. Trigger driven: all three prefill EPs put into 'zerobyte', so connect SUCCEEDS (the stub listens) and the backend then dies mid-request; the deferred re-dispatch reconnects to a re-selected EP successfully, which is what site 686 counts. families.name: loxilb_pd_connect_retry_same_ep_ok_total

writer_sources.note: the success half of the same-endpoint retry pair; retry_total minus this is the failed-retry residual. The gate (sockproxy_ep.c:1053-1070) has three terms and NONE of them reads an engine: ep_cfd < 0 (the initial connect failed), rt_budget > 0 (pd_connect_retry_budget() -- 1 for P/D disagg or KV-exact, 0 for plain LB, a per-rule CONFIG property) and the retry's own connect() >= 0. It is not on the pd_sg_ path at all. The reason it outlived every other pd_* family is narrower than 'hard to reach': no arm had ever produced a connect that FAILS and then SUCCEEDS on the same endpoint, because the retry is in-process and immediate, so the fault has to be count-based at the TCP handshake rather than time-based.

families.verification_evidence: runtime evidence 2026-09-16 (E.5 row 'wp11-connect-retry-ok', WP-11): M08 CPU mock P/D bed (scenario cicd/vllm-kvcache-routing-cpu brought up MON_AIKEY=1, image tag d9b-u24, digest sha256:33b1c5ec698e), harness md5 1f15b550ea86 (verify) / 56503142de20 (backend) / e1cda42a9f79 (swap) / 932492336299 (burst driver), identical at author and bed. 13/13 checks, reproduced on three consecutive runs with zero discarded windows. The LAST non-topology pd_* family. B drives it with an nth-parity REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset on every SECOND SYN reaching the stub port, so a request's initial connect takes ECONNREFUSED and the in-process same-EP retry lands on the very next SYN and connects: delta 3.0 == n, delta pd_connect_retry_same_ep == 3.0 == the same n (the budget is 1, so one attempt per request), 3 'affinity preserved' lines held against the counter in an asserted identity, 3x200 with no receipt, and pd_connect_failover FLAT -- the outcome this family exists to be distinguished from. C IS THE BRANCH ITSELF, NOT SILENCE: with the EPs simply refusing, the retry loop still RUNS, pd_connect_retry_same_ep moves by n and 3 attempt lines are logged, and only the success half is declined; a control where nothing happened could not tell an ATTEMPT counter from a SUCCESS one. The block's two [PD_CONN_RETRY] lines are near collisions by eye ('to preserve affinity' vs 'affinity preserved'), so every stage asserts loose == attempts + oks and the discriminator verifies itself. STAGE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the refusing control runs LAST, because 3 requests x 3 prefill EPs is exactly the breaker trip threshold and running it first meets the drive with 'no healthy prefill candidates' -- selection failing before any connect, which reads identically to 'this family cannot be driven'. THE DRIVE-SHAPE DEFECT THIS ARM CORRECTS IS THE EVIDENCE'S MAIN LESSON. The first version armed ONE nth-parity rule for a whole burst on a measured claim that no other SYN reached the stub port. The claim was false and its measurement had been truncated: the gateway's own vLLM /metrics scraper (pkg/aimetrics.Poller, started per-rule under pdDisaggMode) dials ep.xIP:ep.xPort every 10s, the REDIRECT carries it to the stub port, and at SYN time it is indistinguishable from the data connect. The kernel's rule counter then reported EXACTLY the predicted 3 resets, one per flapped EP, so the drive-shape oracle read as CONFIRMED -- while every reset it had counted was a scrape. The data connects took the accepting slot, succeeded first time, and a WORKING family was reported as a dead one. The fix is a window that states its own shape: the parity is armed FRESH around ONE request with a fall-through witness chain behind the REJECT, so refused+accepted is the total the port saw and a clean window is exactly (1,1); anything else discards the window and re-drives. Red-twinned at the ORACLE, deterministically and in both directions: R1 (REJECT never armed) fails with 'the flap rule pair is incomplete' rather than scoring a flat counter as a product failure, and R2 (--every 1, so the retry is refused too) discards 8 windows and fails with 'no clean single-request window' -- the exact historical failure mode, now caught.

families.verification_evidence: runtime evidence 2026-09-15 (E.5 row 'wp11-sessions', WP-11): M08 CPU mock P/D bed (cicd/vllm-kvcache-routing-cpu), image loxilb-inference-gateway:wp11-u24 sha256:fd072b4b7a0a, custody proven host build md5 83754e4fcb5d == image == md5 inside the RUNNING llb1. READING THE WRITER FIRST CHANGED THE ARM: sockproxy_metrics.c:192 computes this as HASH_COUNT(tepval->pd_session_map) summed over services -- the size of the session STICKINESS map, NOT a count of concurrent in-flight requests. The obvious drive (hold N requests in-flight against a hanging backend and expect the gauge to read N) would have measured a different thing entirely. Entries are inserted by pd_session_store(), whose key comes from exactly two places (sockproxy_ep.c:831-840, mirrored at sockproxy_pd.c:1910-1922): the JSON body 'user' field, and a client-provided X-Conversation-Id header which takes priority and whose 'auto-' prefix is explicitly skipped. With neither present session_key stays NULL and nothing is stored -- which gives this arm an unusually strong control: THE IDENTICAL REQUEST, same body, same endpoints, minus one header, so a flat control cannot be dismissed as flat-for-lack-of-traffic. THREE EXACT PREDICTIONS, ALL MADE FROM SOURCE BEFORE THE RUN AND ALL HELD. CONTROL: 3 requests, no session key, 3x200 -> delta 0.0. DRIVE A: 3 requests with 3 DISTINCT X-Conversation-Id, 3x200 -> delta 3.0 == N, one map entry per distinct key. DRIVE B: 4 requests sharing ONE X-Conversation-Id -> delta 1.0, NOT 4 -- pd_session_store() is an UPSERT (HASH_FIND_STR then update-in-place, sockproxy_pd.c:1147-1166), so M requests on one key add exactly one entry. Drive B is the check that makes this a SESSION gauge rather than a request counter; a delta of M there would mean it counts requests and the name would be wrong. All settles use the same >10 s window as the other WP-11 rows. 7/7 checks. BOUNDS CHECKED so neither can move the gauge under the measurement: PD_SESSION_MAX_ENTRIES 4096 with LRU eviction above it, PD_SESSION_DEFAULT_TTL 300 s. The flip side is recorded deliberately: this gauge does NOT return to baseline when the arm ends, because entries live out their 300 s TTL -- correct behaviour for an affinity map, so the arm does not assert a return to zero; such an assertion would fail against a working product.
